front.title: HyPR: Hybrid Parity for Remote Resilience

abstract.t: Local redundancy mechanisms such as RAID and software-defined parity pools tolerate only a bounded number of correlated device losses, while remote backup services typically require replication of the full data set. HyPR's remote storage requirement scales with the parity-to-data ratio m/k rather than with the size of the protected data, at the cost of not protecting against total loss of the local copy. This document specifies HyPR (Hybrid Parity for Remote Resilience), a framework that treats remote storage, including consumer-grade end-to-end-encrypted cloud services, as additional failure-domain participants in an erasure-coded storage system. HyPR defines a content-chunked Remote Parity Fragment format, transport requirements for backend-agnostic encrypted fragment delivery, immutable and versioned vault semantics, a resumable reconstruction protocol that produces signed rebuild receipts, and a boundary within which machine-learned orchestration agents may advise but never replace deterministic reconstruction.
